meta.label: Glasses and contact lenses
tradeoffLabels: easiest to buy without a store visit
meta.attribution: Covers prescription glasses and contact lenses bought in the US: online-only eyewear sellers, in-store optical chains, a warehouse club, an independent-optometrist network, a nonprofit voucher programme, and the free option of continuing to wear glasses that still match your prescription. Prices here are not perfectly comparable to each other. Some are a single frame's starting price, with lenses priced separately at checkout once a prescription is entered; some are a confirmed complete price for one pair, lenses included; some are a two-pair bundle; and contact lens prices are given per box or as a seller's own annual estimate, because how many boxes a year someone needs depends on the lens type and prescription. Each note says exactly what was confirmed on the page read and what was not. Every seller listed asks for prescription details before completing an order; none of these scores says anything about the quality of anyone's eyesight, only about price and how the product can be bought. Not medical advice; the American Optometric Association's own schedule for eye exam frequency is cited below for people deciding whether a new pair is needed at all. Reviewed 2026-08. Suggest changes via Contribute.

criteria.label: Price for a pair of glasses or a box of contact lenses
States its price online, without a store visit or quote

products.name: Zenni Optical

economical.note: Zenni's own frame-price help page lists frames starting at $6.95, and states that this starting price reflects the frame itself, while adding lenses or protective coatings may add to the cost depending on the prescription. So $6.95 is a starting frame price, not a confirmed complete-pair total.

accessibility.note: Zenni sells online only and ships nationwide, with no membership fee, but the order process requires entering an existing prescription; no eye exam is offered.

transparency.note: Zenni publishes exact frame prices on its own site, including a page of frames all priced at $6.95.

products.description: An online-only eyewear seller with frames starting at $6.95, the cheapest confirmed starting price in this roster, though lens cost is calculated separately once a prescription is entered.

products.name: Payne Glasses

economical.note: Payne Glasses' own homepage advertises '$5.95 Glasses' across its men's, women's and kids' categories, alongside a separate 'FREE Frames' promotion. The homepage does not show a single confirmed complete-pair total including lenses.

accessibility.note: Payne Glasses sells online only, with free shipping over $89 stated on the homepage, no membership fee, and no eye exam offered.

transparency.note: Payne Glasses states its $5.95 frame price directly on its own homepage.

products.description: An online-only eyewear seller advertising $5.95 frames, the lowest headline number in this roster, with lens cost added separately.

products.name: GlassesUSA (glasses)

economical.note: GlassesUSA's own homepage states glasses are 'Starting at just $19' in its 'Glasses on sale' section. The homepage does not confirm whether this starting price includes single-vision lenses.

accessibility.note: GlassesUSA sells online only, ships nationwide, with no membership fee and no eye exam offered; a prescription is entered during ordering.

transparency.note: GlassesUSA states a starting price directly on its own homepage.

products.description: An online-only eyewear seller advertising glasses starting at $19, the highest of the three online frame-only starting prices in this roster.

products.name: GlassesUSA (contact lenses)

economical.note: GlassesUSA's own contact lens page states 'someone with a standard prescription should pay somewhere between $250-$550 for a year's worth of contacts', its own estimate rather than a single box price, since cost depends on lens type and how many boxes a year the prescription needs.

accessibility.note: GlassesUSA sells contact lenses online with no membership fee; prescription information is required to complete an order.

transparency.note: GlassesUSA discloses a cost estimate for a year's supply directly on its own contact lens page, rather than requiring a store visit for a quote, though it does not show an exact box price on that page.

products.description: GlassesUSA's own estimate for a year of contact lenses on a standard prescription, priced as a range rather than a single box, sold online with no membership fee.

products.name: Eyeconic

economical.note: Eyeconic's own homepage states 'High-quality glasses in trendy shapes and colors from $139. Yes, that price includes your prescription lenses,' a confirmed complete-pair price including lenses, the highest confirmed complete single-pair price in this roster.

accessibility.note: Eyeconic sells online, and its homepage states VSP vision insurance is optional: 'No coverage? Ask your employer or check out a VSP Individual Vision Plan,' with a further 20 per cent off for people who do have VSP benefits linked. No physical visit is required to buy.

transparency.note: Eyeconic states its $139 complete price, including prescription lenses, directly on its own homepage, describing its pricing as 'what you see is what you pay.'

products.description: VSP's online eyewear seller, with a confirmed complete price of $139 including prescription lenses, usable with or without VSP vision insurance.

products.name: Stanton Optical

economical.note: Stanton Optical's own homepage advertises a '2-Pair Bundle, $79, FREE Eye Exam, FREE Single-Vision Lenses,' a confirmed complete price for two pairs including the exam and lenses, about $39.50 per pair.

accessibility.note: Stanton Optical requires an in-person store visit, but the eye exam is included free with the bundle rather than needing a separate appointment or fee, and the chain has locations nationwide.

transparency.note: Stanton Optical states its $79 two-pair bundle price directly on its own homepage.

products.description: An in-store optical chain advertising two complete pairs with a free eye exam for $79, the cheapest confirmed complete price per pair in this roster, but requiring a store visit.

products.name: MyEyeDr

economical.note: MyEyeDr's own homepage states 'Get a Complete Pair for Just $95' and 'Designer frames for just $169. Complete pairs for $95,' a confirmed complete price for one pair, higher per pair than the two-pair bundles offered by America's Best and Stanton Optical.

accessibility.note: MyEyeDr requires an in-person store visit; its homepage promotes savings through vision insurance ('Vision insurance covers your eye exam!') rather than stating a free exam is included without insurance.

transparency.note: MyEyeDr states its $95 complete-pair price directly on its own homepage.

products.description: An in-store optical chain with a confirmed complete price of $95 for one pair, the most expensive confirmed complete single-pair price in the in-store part of this roster, and an eye exam that its own homepage ties to insurance coverage rather than stating it is free.

products.name: America's Best (glasses)

economical.note: America's Best's own offer page states '2 PAIRS OF GLASSES + EYE EXAM FOR $95,' and that this 'includes single-vision, uncoated plastic lenses, frames tagged at $79.95, and a free eye exam,' a confirmed complete price for two pairs plus the exam, about $47.50 per pair. Upgrades to frames, coatings or lens types cost more, and the offer cannot be combined with insurance.

accessibility.note: America's Best requires an in-person store visit for this offer, but the comprehensive eye exam is included at no extra cost rather than needing a separate paid visit; exams without the two-pair purchase are $80 on their own.

transparency.note: America's Best states its $95 two-pair-plus-exam price directly on its own offer page.

products.description: A budget in-store chain bundling two complete pairs of single-vision glasses with a free eye exam for $95, requiring a store visit.

products.name: America's Best (contact lenses)

economical.note: America's Best's own contact lens page lists box prices including 'As low as $56.69 / $62.99 /box' for Sofmed Breathables XW and 'As low as $38.69 / $42.99 /box' for Sofmed Advanced, its own store-brand lenses; a separate 30 per cent off coupon code is offered for eyeglasses on the same page.

accessibility.note: America's Best sells contact lenses with prices and a filter tool shown directly on its own website; a valid prescription is required to complete an order.

transparency.note: America's Best publishes exact box prices for individual contact lens products directly on its own site.

products.description: America's Best's own store-brand contact lenses, with per-box prices published on its site starting near $38.69 for its cheapest listed lens.

products.name: Costco Optical

accessibility.note: Costco's own online eyeglasses FAQ states an active Costco membership and a Costco.com account are required to order, that Costco.com currently offers only single-vision and non-prescription lenses, and that bifocal, progressive or 'BAL' lenses can only be ordered through the Optical Department inside a physical warehouse.

transparency.note: Costco's own online eyeglasses FAQ does not state a price or price range anywhere on the page.

products.description: Costco's optical department, open only to paying Costco members; its own FAQ page does not publish a price, and full lens options require a warehouse visit rather than online ordering. A checkable price was not found on the pages read for this decision, so it is left out rather than guessed.

products.name: Independent optometrist (Vision Source network)

accessibility.note: Vision Source describes itself on its own homepage as a 'Premier Network of Independent Optometrists,' directing visitors to find a local doctor; buying glasses or contacts this way always means an in-person visit to that practice rather than an online order.

transparency.note: Vision Source's own homepage contains no price, cost range or fee information for any practice in its network.

products.description: A local independent optometrist, represented here by the Vision Source network; price varies by practice and is not published centrally, and buying this way always means an in-person visit. A checkable price was not found for this decision, so it is left out rather than guessed.

products.name: New Eyes voucher programme

economical.note: New Eyes' own site describes 'Providing new prescription eyeglasses and clear vision to over 500,000 financially struggling children and adults across the United States' through a voucher system, at no cost to the qualifying recipient.

accessibility.note: New Eyes' own site describes helping people whose 'family can't afford to buy glasses' and references an application and voucher process, meaning this route requires demonstrating financial need and applying rather than being available to any shopper on demand; the site did not state specific income thresholds on the page read.

products.description: A US nonprofit that provides prescription eyeglasses at no cost through a voucher system to people who show financial need, rather than to any shopper who asks.

products.name: Keep wearing your current glasses

economical.note: No product to buy, so no cost, as long as the existing prescription still matches the eyes it was written for.

accessibility.note: NIH's National Eye Institute states how often a dilated eye exam is needed depends on individual risk, giving examples such as every one to two years for people over 60 or with a family history of glaucoma, and at least once a year for people with diabetes or high blood pressure. The American Optometric Association's own recommended schedule for asymptomatic, low-risk adults is 'at least every two years' for ages 18 to 64, and 'annually' from 65. Between exams, a person whose vision has not changed can keep wearing glasses they already own.
